title: Cross-Validation
objectives: Explain the key ideas behind Cross-Validation.
Describe why Cross-Validation matters in Data Science.
Apply Cross-Validation to a realistic scenario.
Identify common pitfalls and how to avoid them.
definition: Cross-Validation is a core concept in Data Science. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What Cross-Validation is
theory.body: Cross-Validation describes the methods and patterns used within Data Science to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Cross-Validation is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Cross-Validation matters
theory.body: Without Cross-Validation, systems built with Data Science are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Cross-Validation works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Cross-Validation follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Cross-Validation.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Cross-Validation
theory.body: Cross-Validation offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
